q_en: How do “as for … then”, “either … or”, “when”, “while”, “whenever” and “until” tie sentences together?
q_ar: كَيْفَ تَرْبِطُ «أَمَّا» وَ«إِمَّا» وَ«لَمَّا» وَ«كُلَّمَا» الْجُمَلَ؟
not_yet: The meaning of لَمَّا as “not yet”, and فَـ after other words.
How a verb changes its ending after حَتَّى and أَنْ (Lesson 69).
not_yet_ar: قَاعِدَةُ «لَمَّا» بِمَعْنَى «لَمْ … بَعْدُ» وَالْفَاءِ بَعْدَ كَلِمَاتٍ أُخْرَى.
كَيْفَ يَتَغَيَّرُ آخِرُ الْفِعْلِ بَعْدَ «حَتَّى» وَ«أَنْ» (الدَّرْسُ ٦٩).

sents: As for the lesson, it is easy.
هُوَ إِمَّا فِي الْمَسْجِدِ وَإِمَّا فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ.
He is either in the mosque or in the library.
Ahmad sat until the Habib came.
When the Habib entered, the students sat.
بَيْنَمَا كَانَ أَحْمَدُ يَقْرَأُ جَاءَ عُمَرُ.
While Ahmad was reading, ʿUmar came.
كُلَّمَا قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ فَهِمَ شَيْئًا جَدِيدًا.
Whenever the boy reads, he understands something new.

lines: Which word comes first in each sentence? What does it join to what?
أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَأْتِي أَوَّلًا فِي كُلِّ جُمْلَةٍ؟ وَمَاذَا تَرْبِطُ؟
In the first sentence, look for the small letter فَـ. Where does it stand?
فِي الْجُمْلَةِ الْأُولَى: أَيْنَ الْحَرْفُ الصَّغِيرُ «فَـ»؟
Which sentences tell you WHEN? Which tell you WHICH ONE of two?
أَيُّ الْجُمَلِ تَقُولُ: مَتَى؟ وَأَيُّهَا تَقُولُ: أَيُّ وَاحِدٍ مِنِ اثْنَيْنِ؟

cards.def_ar: اِذْكُرِ الْمَوْضُوعَ، وَمَا يُقَالُ عَنْهُ يَبْدَأُ بِفَـ.
cards.def_en: Name the topic. What is said about it begins with فَـ.
Two choices. Each has its own إِمَّا (or: إِمَّا … أَوْ).

cards.def_ar: لَمَّا: مَرَّةً وَاحِدَةً. بَيْنَمَا: فِي الْوَقْتِ نَفْسِهِ. كُلَّمَا: فِي كُلِّ مَرَّةٍ. وَبَعْدَهَا فِعْلٌ مَاضٍ.
cards.def_en: once · at the same time · every time. A past verb follows.

cards.def_ar: إِلَى أَنْ. وَبَعْدَهَا هُنَا فِعْلٌ مَاضٍ: يَتَوَقَّفُ الْعَمَلُ حِينَ يَحْدُثُ.
cards.def_en: until. Here a past verb follows: it stops when it happened.

slides.note: The first four rows you knew. The rest is new today.
slides.note_ar: الصُّفُوفُ الْأَرْبَعَةُ الْأُولَى مَعْرُوفَةٌ. وَالْبَاقِي جَدِيدٌ الْيَوْمَ.

slides.tip: When + a past verb is one word. “Did not” + the present form is another.
slides.tip_ar: بَعْدَ «لَمَّا» فِعْلٌ مَاضٍ. بَعْدَ «لَمْ» فِعْلٌ مُضَارِعٌ وَالْمَعْنَى نَفْيٌ.

slides.head_en: Try: what does the joining word say?

slides.why: A student writes this for “As for the wird, do not leave it”. Wrong! After the topic of أَمَّا, the next part begins with فَـ: أَمَّا الْوِرْدُ فَلَا تَتْرُكْهُ.
slides.why_ar: كَتَبَ طَالِبٌ هَذِهِ الْجُمْلَةَ. هَذَا خَطَأٌ! بَعْدَ مَوْضُوعِ «أَمَّا» يَبْدَأُ الْكَلَامُ عَنْهُ بِـ «فَـ»: أَمَّا الْوِرْدُ فَلَا تَتْرُكْهُ.

lines: أَمَّا بَعْدُ، فَإِنَّا انْتَظَرْنَا رِسَالَتَكَ يَوْمًا بَعْدَ يَوْمٍ حَتَّى وَصَلَتْ.
To proceed: we waited for your letter day after day until it arrived.
And I am very happy with it.
أَمَّا الدَّرْسُ فَاقْرَأْهُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ، وَأَمَّا الْوِرْدُ فَلَا تَتْرُكْهُ أَبَدًا.
As for the lesson, read it every day, and as for the wird, never leave it.
وَكُلَّمَا قَرَأْتَ شَيْئًا جَدِيدًا فَاكْتُبْهُ فِي كِتَابِكَ.
And whenever you read something new, write it in your book.
اِجْلِسْ إِمَّا فِي الْمَسْجِدِ وَإِمَّا فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ، وَلَا تَجْلِسْ فِي الشَّارِعِ.
Sit either in the mosque or in the library, and do not sit in the street.
وَبَيْنَمَا كُنْتُ أَقْرَأُ رِسَالَتَكَ جَاءَ الضُّيُوفُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ.
And while I was reading your letter, the guests came to the house.
وَلَمَّا جَاءَ الْإِخْوَانُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ سَلَّمُوا عَلَيْكَ.
And when the brothers came to the ribāṭ, they greeted you.
أَمَّا بَعْدُ : فَاعْلَمُوا مَعَاشِرَ الْإِخْوَانِ فِي الدِّينِ ، وَالْأَعْوَانِ عَلَى طَاعَةِ اللهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ
To proceed: know, brothers in religion and helpers in obeying God, Lord of the worlds,
كُلَّمَا خَلِقَ وَكَادَ أَنْ تَنْطَمِسَ مَعَالِمُهُ ، وَتَذْهَبَ طَرَاوَتُهُ وَجِدَّتُهُ
Every time it wears out and its landmarks almost fade, and its freshness and newness go.
slides.source: Mukātabāt al-Imām al-Ḥaddād (Jāmiʿ al-Mukātabāt wa-l-Waṣāyā wa-l-Kalimāt wa-l-Qaṣāʾid), vol. 1 (vowelled for learners)

lines: وَأَمَّا الصَّوْمُ: وَهُوَ الثَّالِثُ مِنْ أَرْكَانِ الْإِسْلَامِ، فَهُوَ إِمْسَاكٌ مَعْرُوفٌ
As for fasting, the third pillar of Islam, it is a well-known abstention.
وَأَمَّا الْحَجُّ: فَهُوَ خَامِسُ أَرْكَانِ الْإِسْلَامِ
As for the pilgrimage, it is the fifth pillar of Islam.
slides.source: al-Risāla al-Jāmiʿa wa-l-Tadhkira al-Nāfiʿa of Imām Aḥmad b. Zayn al-Ḥabashī (1069–1145 AH)

lines: As for the orphan, do not oppress him.
And as for the one who asks, do not scold him.
And as for the blessing of your Lord, tell of it.

can: I can read أَمَّا … فَـ and say what the topic is and what is said about it.
I can tell إِمَّا … وَإِمَّا (a choice) from لَمَّا, بَيْنَمَا and كُلَّمَا (time) and read the verb after them.
I can read the opening أَمَّا بَعْدُ of a letter.
can_ar: أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ «أَمَّا … فَـ» وَأَقُولَ مَا الْمَوْضُوعُ وَمَاذَا يُقَالُ عَنْهُ.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أُمَيِّزَ «إِمَّا … وَإِمَّا» (اخْتِيَارٌ) مِنْ «لَمَّا» وَ«بَيْنَمَا» وَ«كُلَّمَا» (زَمَانٌ) وَأَقْرَأَ الْفِعْلَ بَعْدَهَا.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ «أَمَّا بَعْدُ» فِي أَوَّلِ الرِّسَالَةِ.

sections.name: A
sections.en: Read the letter, then answer. (★ rows are for adults and older students.)
lines: أَمَّا بَعْدُ، فَإِنَّا انْتَظَرْنَا رِسَالَتَكَ يَوْمًا بَعْدَ يَوْمٍ حَتَّى وَصَلَتْ.
To proceed: we waited for your letter day after day until it arrived.
And I am very happy with it.
أَمَّا الدَّرْسُ فَاقْرَأْهُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ، وَأَمَّا الْوِرْدُ فَلَا تَتْرُكْهُ أَبَدًا.
As for the lesson, read it every day, and as for the wird, never leave it.
وَكُلَّمَا قَرَأْتَ شَيْئًا جَدِيدًا فَاكْتُبْهُ فِي كِتَابِكَ.
And whenever you read something new, write it in your book.
اِجْلِسْ إِمَّا فِي الْمَسْجِدِ وَإِمَّا فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ، وَلَا تَجْلِسْ فِي الشَّارِعِ.
Sit either in the mosque or in the library, and do not sit in the street.
وَبَيْنَمَا كُنْتُ أَقْرَأُ رِسَالَتَكَ جَاءَ الضُّيُوفُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ.
And while I was reading your letter, the guests came to the house.
وَلَمَّا جَاءَ الْإِخْوَانُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ سَلَّمُوا عَلَيْكَ.
And when the brothers came to the ribāṭ, they greeted you.
sections.cite: Course text (a letter from the uncle), written for this lesson. Words of Lessons 1–67 and the extra words of Lessons 66–67 only.
sections.teacher_note: ★ rows are for adults and older students; children may skip them.

options: Guests came to the house; بَيْنَمَا.
The brothers, when they came to the ribāṭ; لَمَّا.

items.en: With which words does the letter begin, and what do they mean?
items.ar_q: بِأَيِّ كَلِمَاتٍ تَبْدَأُ الرِّسَالَةُ؟ وَمَاذَا تَعْنِي؟
items.model: أَمَّا بَعْدُ: “to proceed”. It is how a letter moves from the greeting to its subject.

items.en: How long did they wait for Ahmad’s letter, and until when?
options: Read the lesson every day; never leave the wird.
In the mosque or in the library; not in the street.
Day after day, until it arrived
items.answer: Day after day, until it arrived
items.model: Day after day, until it arrived (حَتَّى وَصَلَتْ).

items.en: What does the uncle say about the lesson? And about the wird?
items.ar_q: مَاذَا يَقُولُ عَنِ الدَّرْسِ؟ وَعَنِ الْوِرْدِ؟
options: Read the lesson every day; never leave the wird.
In the mosque or in the library; not in the street.
Day after day, until it arrived
items.answer: Read the lesson every day; never leave the wird.
items.model: Read the lesson every day; never leave the wird.

items.en: In line 3 the uncle speaks about two topics. How many أَمَّا are there, and what follows each one?
items.ar_q: فِي السَّطْرِ ٣ مَوْضُوعَانِ. كَمْ «أَمَّا» فِيهِ؟ وَمَاذَا بَعْدَ كُلٍّ مِنْهُمَا؟
items.model: Two. Each topic (الدَّرْسُ، الْوِرْدُ) is followed by فَـ and the advice.

items.en: What must Ahmad do whenever he reads something new?
items.ar_q: مَاذَا يَفْعَلُ أَحْمَدُ كُلَّمَا قَرَأَ شَيْئًا جَدِيدًا؟
options: Day after day, until it arrived
Read the lesson every day; never leave the wird.
In the mosque or in the library; not in the street.
items.model: Write it in his book (كُلَّمَا … فَاكْتُبْهُ).

items.en: Where may Ahmad sit, and where not?
items.ar_q: أَيْنَ يَجْلِسُ أَحْمَدُ؟ وَأَيْنَ لَا يَجْلِسُ؟
options: In the mosque or in the library; not in the street.
Day after day, until it arrived
Read the lesson every day; never leave the wird.
items.answer: In the mosque or in the library; not in the street.
items.model: In the mosque or in the library; not in the street.

items.en: What happened while the uncle was reading? Which word says “while”?
items.ar_q: مَاذَا حَدَثَ؟ وَأَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَقُولُ إِنَّ الْحَدَثَيْنِ فِي وَقْتٍ وَاحِدٍ؟
options: The brothers, when they came to the ribāṭ; لَمَّا.
Guests came to the house; بَيْنَمَا.
items.answer: Guests came to the house; بَيْنَمَا.
items.model: Guests came to the house; بَيْنَمَا.

items.en: Who greeted Ahmad, and when? Which word says “when”?
items.ar_q: مَنْ سَلَّمَ عَلَى أَحْمَدَ؟ وَأَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى الْوَقْتِ؟
options: Guests came to the house; بَيْنَمَا.
The brothers, when they came to the ribāṭ; لَمَّا.
items.answer: The brothers, when they came to the ribāṭ; لَمَّا.
items.model: The brothers, when they came to the ribāṭ; لَمَّا.

items.en: True or false? The uncle says: “Sit only in the mosque.”
items.model: False. إِمَّا … وَإِمَّا = either … or: the mosque or the library.
items.note: إِمَّا … وَإِمَّا = either … or: the mosque or the library.

items.en: How does the uncle end the letter?
items.model: With a prayer, اللَّهُ يَحْفَظُكَ (“May Allah protect you”), and his name.

items.en: ★ In line 1, بَعْدُ ends with ـُ and has no tanwīn. What is different from بَعْدَ in “after the lesson”?
items.model: In this fixed phrase the word after it is left out in the mind, so بَعْدُ keeps a plain ـُ.

items.en: ★ In line 6, كُنْتُ comes before أَقْرَأُ. What does this give to the meaning?
items.model: “I was reading”: the action was going on when the guests came. This is the usual shape after بَيْنَمَا.

items.en: What are the two topics, one in each line?
Which place in the order of the pillars does each one have?
items.model: Fasting is the third (الثَّالِثُ); the pilgrimage is the fifth (خَامِسُ).
As for the pilgrimage, it is the fifth pillar of Islam.

items.en: ★ Each line begins with وَأَمَّا and later has فَـ (فَهُوَ). What does the فَـ do?
items.model: It begins what is said about the topic: “as for fasting, … then it is …”.

items.en: ★ Each line begins with وَأَمَّا, “and as for”. Why “and”?
items.model: The lines belong to a list of the pillars: each topic follows the one before and is joined to it by وَ.

sections.name: D
sections.en: Three verses. (Words: تَقْهَرْ = oppress, تَنْهَرْ = scold.) Read aloud, then answer.

items.en: A student translates this: “When Ahmad went”. What is wrong?
items.model: لَمْ + the present form means “did not”: Ahmad did not go. “When Ahmad went” is لَمَّا ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ.

items.ar: هُوَ إِمَّا فِي الْمَسْجِدِ فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ.
items.model: إِمَّا needs its partner: إِمَّا … وَإِمَّا (or أَوْ): هُوَ إِمَّا فِي الْمَسْجِدِ وَإِمَّا فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ.

items.en: A student translates this: “He read once and understood.” What is wrong?

سَأَلَ عُمَرُ صَدِيقَهُ: هَلْ أَنْتَ ذَاهِبٌ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ؟
Umar asked his friend: Are you going to the rawḥa?
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: الصَّلَاةُ نُورٌ.
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Prayer is light.
The boy opened his muṣḥaf and read his wird (his daily portion).
صَلَّى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الطُّلَّابِ ثُمَّ دَعَا.
The boy prayed with the students, then made duʿāʾ.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الْمَوْلِدَ لِأَنَّ مَحَبَّةَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ فِي قَلْبِهِ.
The boy read the mawlid because love of the Prophet ﷺ is in his heart.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ لِأَبِي الْوَلَدِ: وَلَدُكَ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ.
The Habib said to the boy’s father: Your son is a student of knowledge (ṭālib ʿilm).
جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي مَجَالِسِ الْعُلَمَاءِ فِي تَرِيمَ.
The boy sat in the gatherings of the scholars in Tarim.
يُقَالُ إِنَّ الْإِمَامَ وُلِدَ فِي تَرِيمَ.
It is said that the Imam was born in Tarim.
It was said to the boy: Knowledge is light.
عَلَّمَ الْحَبِيبُ الْوَلَدَ: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ عَلَى سَيِّدِنَا مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ.
The Habib taught the boy: O Allah, bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad ﷺ.
The boy reminded his friend of the prayer.
فِي اللَّيْلِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَصْحَابِ وَقَرَأَ الرَّاتِبَ.
At night the boy sat with the companions and read the Rātib.
قَالُوا: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ.
They said: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and Allah is greater.
فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ مَعَ أَبِيهِ.
On the Night of Qadr the boy sat in the mosque with his father.
The boy helped the guests and honoured them.
The students helped one another in the ribāṭ.
The boy was humble and learned from them.
اِنْتَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ الْحَبِيبَ عِنْدَ بَابِ الْمَسْجِدِ.
The boy waited for the Habib at the door of the mosque.
اِجْتَمَعَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ وَاسْتَمَعَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْحَبِيبِ.
The students gathered in the morning and the boy listened to the Habib.
حَجَّ أَبُو الْوَلَدِ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ مِنْ مَكَّةَ.
The boy’s father made the pilgrimage, then returned from Mecca.
أَخَذَ الْوَلَدُ التَّمْرَ مِنْ أَبِيهِ وَقَدَّمَهُ لِلضُّيُوفِ.
The boy took the dates from his father and offered them to the guests.
The boy heard a ḥadīth with its chain.
قَالَ الرَّاوِي: حَدَّثَنَا وَأَخْبَرَنَا، ثُمَّ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ.
The narrator said: He told us, and he informed us, then the Prophet ﷺ said: Deeds are only by intentions.
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: قُلْ آمَنْتُ بِاللَّهِ فَاسْتَقِمْ.
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Say: I believe in Allah, and then be upright.
The boy stood up and said: I believe in Allah.
مَشَى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ وَوَصَلَ فِي الْمَسَاءِ.
The boy walked with his father to the ziyāra and arrived in the evening.
The boy made duʿāʾ: O Allah, guide us.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَقَالَ: مَا أَحْسَنَ هَذَا الْمَجْلِسَ!
The boy came to the majlis and said: How beautiful this majlis is!
قَالَ لِأُمِّهِ: جِئْتُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَرَأَيْتُ الْحَبِيبَ.
He said to his mother: I came to the majlis and I saw the Habib.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ كَلِمَاتٍ مِنْ جَذْرٍ وَاحِدٍ: عَلَّمَ، مُعَلِّمٌ، تَعْلِيمٌ.
The boy wrote words from one root: ʿallama, muʿallim, taʿlīm.
And he wrote: sāfara, musāfir, safar.
نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى مِنْبَرِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَمِحْرَابِهِ.
The boy looked at the minbar of the mosque and its miḥrāb.
قَالَ الْوَلَدُ: أَنَا حَضْرَمِيٌّ مِنْ تَرِيمَ.
The boy said: I am a Ḥaḍramī, from Tarim.
نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ بِنَفْسِهِ فِي الْمُعْجَمِ وَوَجَدَ مَعْنَى الْكَلِمَةِ.
The boy looked in the dictionary by himself and found the meaning of the word.
ثُمَّ كَتَبَ الْجَذْرَ وَالْمَعْنَى فِي كِتَابِهِ.
Then he wrote the root and the meaning in his book.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ مَتْنًا صَغِيرًا.
The boy read a small matn (a short base text) with the Habib.
أَصْبَحَ الْمَتْنُ سَهْلًا لَكِنَّ الدَّرْسَ طَوِيلٌ.
The matn became easy, but the lesson is long.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الدَّرْسِ مُسْرِعًا وَجَلَسَ مُسْتَقْبِلَ الْقِبْلَةِ.
The boy came to the lesson hurrying, and sat facing the qibla.
And the Habib was pleased with him.
ذَكَرَ الْوَلَدُ اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا وَصَلَّى عَلَى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ ثَلَاثًا.
The boy remembered Allah a great deal and prayed for blessings on the Prophet ﷺ three times.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ مَرَّتَيْنِ طَلَبًا لِلْعِلْمِ.
The boy read the lesson twice, seeking knowledge.
The Habib gave the boy a small book.
ظَنَّ الْوَلَدُ الْكِتَابَ صَعْبًا فَقَالَ: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ.
The boy thought the book difficult, so he said: There is no power and no strength except through Allah.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ أَرْكَانَ الْوُضُوءِ: الْأَوَّلُ النِّيَّةُ، وَالثَّانِي غَسْلُ الْوَجْهِ.
The boy wrote the pillars of the ablution: the first, the intention; and the second, washing the face.
وَالثَّالِثُ غَسْلُ الْيَدَيْنِ، وَالرَّابِعُ مَسْحُ بَعْضِ الرَّأْسِ.
And the third, washing the hands; and the fourth, wiping part of the head.
The boy read the wird in the morning.
ثُمَّ دَعَا: يَا رَبِّ، اِهْدِنَا وَاعْفُ عَنَّا، آمِينَ.
Then he made duʿāʾ: O my Lord, guide us and pardon us. Amen.
شَرِبَ الْوَلَدُ مِنْ مَاءِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَمَا شَرِبَ إِلَّا مَاءً طَاهِرًا.
The boy drank from the water of the mosque, and he drank only pure water.
Neither its colour nor its taste had changed.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ اِسْمَ الشَّيْخِ عَلَى الْكِتَابِ: سَالِمُ بْنُ يُوسُفَ.
The boy read the shaykh’s name on the book: Salim son of Yusuf.
And his kunya is Abū Aḥmad.
رَغِبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْعِلْمِ وَالْأَجْرِ وَرَغِبَ عَنِ الْإِثْمِ.
The boy desired knowledge and reward, and turned away from sin.
فَقَالَ لَهُ الْحَبِيبُ: لَا تَرْغَبْ فِي الدُّنْيَا.
So the Habib said to him: Do not set your desire on this world.
اِسْتَيْقَظَ الْوَلَدُ قَبْلَ الْفَجْرِ وَأَخَذَ السِّوَاكَ.
The boy woke up before dawn and took the siwāk.
Then he sat and strove in his wird.
The boy never missed the rawḥa.
يَحْضُرُ الْوَلَدُ الرَّوْحَةَ دَائِمًا وَهُوَ سَعِيدٌ جِدًّا.
The boy always attends the rawḥa, and he is very happy.
A letter arrived from the boy’s uncle.
بَدَأَ الْعَمُّ رِسَالَتَهُ: أَمَّا بَعْدُ، فَاطْلُبِ الْعِلْمَ.
The uncle began his letter: Now then, seek knowledge.
